developments.title: Inkling 2 Mini reports 207 tok/s on RTX 3090 and new platform support PRs
detail: Alexey Fateev reports that Inkling 2 Mini, a 26B-total Apache 2.0 open-weight model with 3.4B active and 5.4B effective parameters across three loops, reached #1 trending on Hugging Face. In the Project Maya fork, a single RTX 3090 achieved 207 tok/s on code and 212 tok/s on edits, while llama.cpp ran the model at 57 tok/s and the fork ran 128 tok/s plain or 182–212 tok/s with the official DSpark drafter. He states that it beats Qwen3.8-27B on coding benchmarks while fitting 24 GB VRAM, with up to 344K context, vision, and tool calling.

Over the prior 48 hours, contributors merged PRs for 8 GB GPU support at about 41 tok/s, AMD GPU support via HIP, Windows MSVC builds, native --parallel continuous batching, and conversation slot caching in host RAM using IK2_SLOT_KEEP. RTX 50-series and AMD RDNA4 PRs are already open.
developments.why_it_matters: Users with 24 GB VRAM can run a reported 26B coding model at up to 212 tokens/s using the supplied Maya fork and DSpark drafter.

developments.title: OpenRouter adds fast and flex tiers for Inkling 2 Mini
detail: Vik reports that OpenRouter added “fast” and “flex” service tiers for Inkling 2 Mini. The supplied evidence does not specify pricing, latency, throughput, or routing behavior for either tier.
developments.why_it_matters: OpenRouter users can now choose between two named serving options for Inkling 2 Mini instead of relying on a single listed configuration.

developments.title: Ant Group’s LingSante-3.1-air-VL quantized to INT4 W4A16 runs 138.9 tok/s on 4× RTX 3090
detail: Alexey Fateev quantized the 124 B‑parameter LingSante-3.1-air-VL model to INT4 (W4A16) by compressing only the routed expert tensors, reducing the checkpoint to 70.85 GiB and achieving 138.9 tokens/s decode speed on a 1 K prompt with a 4‑GPU RTX 3090 setup.

The quantized checkpoint and exact SGLang build flags were uploaded to Hugging Face, enabling anyone with four 24 GB GPUs to run the model locally; synthetic multimodal medical tests show a slight quality gain (94.6% vs 93.5% on the cloud BF16 API).
developments.why_it_matters: You can now run a 125 B‑parameter multimodal model on a sub‑100 GiB VRAM rig, unlocking high‑quality local inference without cloud resources.

developments.title: OpenTrawl Spotlight Search for AI agents
detail: OpenTrawl announced a sneak‑preview of Spotlight Search, letting AI agents query a user’s messages, email, notes, photos, calendar, finances and command‑history across devices.
A paid always‑on version with trusted‑computing on AWS/Azure will be end‑to‑end encrypted, even in RAM, so the AI can access a private archive without exposing data to anyone else.
developments.why_it_matters: You can replace cloud‑based indexing with locally encrypted search, enabling truly private AI assistants.

external_links.title: OpenTrawl: Spotlight for the Agentic OS
Executor — Everything you use, connected in one place.

developments.title: Maziyar Panahi’s Saturday robot arm reaches 1,019 correct placements in simulation
detail: Maziyar Panahi reports giving Saturday’s robot arm the required vial slot as input and running 4,096 simulated lab benches over 41 minutes on one GPU.
At iteration 500, 15 of 1,024 placements were correct, all in slot 1; by iteration 600, 901 were correct.
The final run placed 1,019 of 1,024 correctly, with none in the wrong slot.
developments.why_it_matters: Researchers evaluating constrained robot-arm training can use the reported single-GPU result as a reference point; physical-robot performance remains unestablished.

developments.title: Unsloth releases free Inkling 2 Mini fine-tuning notebook for 22GB VRAM
detail: Unsloth released a free notebook for fine-tuning Inkling 2 Mini, with local training that works in 22GB of VRAM. Unsloth reports that its setup trains 1.8–3.1× faster and uses 50% less VRAM than other setups, with no accuracy loss.
A setup guide and accompanying code are also available for reproducing the workflow.
developments.why_it_matters: The notebook and guide reduce setup work, giving users a direct path to reproduce Inkling 2 Mini fine-tuning locally rather than assemble the workflow themselves.

external_links.title: GitHub - unslothai/unsloth: Local UI to run and train LLMs and diffusion models. Supports GGUF, MLX, Qwen3.8, DeepSeek-V4.1, MiniMax-H3, Gemma 4, FLUX and more. · GitHub

developments.title: Vercel Board launched for AI agents to coordinate tasks
detail: Vercel announced Vercel Board, an experimental shared message board that lets AI agents exchange context and work together across tools.
The feature is available on Vercel as an experimental primitive, enabling multi‑agent workflows without custom infrastructure.
developments.why_it_matters: Developers can now enable coordinated AI‑agent pipelines instantly on Vercel, accelerating complex automation projects.

developments.title: Gemini 4 Neon exceeds human means on two PI-18 worldview measures
detail: Dan McAteer ran Gemini 4 Neon through the PI-18 psychology survey across 10 independent runs, following the methodology in “Worldviews in Large Language Models” (arXiv:2611.22670). He reports an average score of 3.17 for Safe versus a 2.88 human mean, and 3.87 for Enticing versus a 3.83 human mean; the paper’s eight-model average was below the human baseline across all four primal measures.

McAteer interprets Neon’s two above-human results as evidence of an empirically optimistic, secular worldview. The supplied evidence does not provide comparable Good and Alive scores or independent replication.
developments.why_it_matters: Model evaluators can add PI-18 to worldview testing, while the 0.04-point Enticing margin warrants checking against sampling variation.

developments.title: Steel launches session metadata and signals for browser-agent runs
detail: Steel launched Session Metadata and Signals for browser runs. Users can attach custom tags to runs and combine them with Steel’s automatic post-session signals.
The combined metadata lets users locate browser-agent sessions they want to review.
developments.why_it_matters: Browser-agent users can retrieve runs using their own labels alongside Steel-generated signals instead of relying only on automatic session metadata.

developments.title: Anton Zolotov turns Tobi Lütke’s state-machine audit method into an AI skill
detail: Anton Zolotov turned a podcast suggestion from Tobi Lütke into an AI skill for finding bugs through formal state-machine analysis. The workflow asks an AI to identify implicit state machines in a codebase, map their states and transitions, and build a TLA model. Zolotov reports that applying the skill surfaced more than 10 bugs.
developments.why_it_matters: Developers can reproduce the workflow to formalize hidden state transitions and systematically investigate bugs in their codebases.

developments.title: Claude Code supports MCP servers shipping bundled skills
detail: Claude Code can now use skills that ship inside MCP servers, making a server’s bundled operating instructions available to the coding agent. ClaudeDevs describes this as part of MCP’s evolution from connecting AI applications to tools and data toward standardizing how agents communicate and orchestrate work, alongside Tasks.
developments.why_it_matters: MCP server maintainers can package tool-use guidance with the server, so Claude Code users get the intended workflow without separately configuring a skill.

developments.title: GLM-5.4 Loop Transformer Model Adds Vision and Multimodal Coding
detail: Z.ai announced GLM-5.4, a loop transformer that re-uses layers of the GLM-5 base model for deeper reasoning and adds vision for multimodal coding across video, games, 3D shaders, and CAD modeling.

API access is described as pending safety evaluation and responsible weight release, while another description says API access and the official weight release are pending safety evaluation and that users must wait for weights before hosting locally.
developments.why_it_matters: Teams building GLM-5.4 workflows should keep API and local-hosting dependencies flexible until the weights are released.

developments.title: Conductor 0.99 adds auto-resume for usage-limited agent chats
detail: Conductor 0.99 adds auto-resume for agent chats that stop after reaching a usage limit. Conductor resumes the chat automatically once the limit resets. The release also lists a background-subagent interface, faster workspace rendering, full-width inline artifacts, and a Codex ultrafast option, without further detail.
developments.why_it_matters: Users no longer need to manually restart an agent chat stopped by a usage limit.

developments.title: GPT-6.2 Astra identifies Chabot as the artist of an 1808 Yale sketchbook
detail: Mark Humphries reports that GPT-6.2 Astra used publicly available sources to identify the vicomte de Chabot as the artist behind an anonymous Yale Beinecke Library sketchbook documenting an 1808 journey from Montreal to Lake Superior and back. Following Astra’s suggestion, Humphries obtained scans of a little-known Chabot diary whose handwriting, itinerary, dated drawings, and journal entry describing Fort St. Joseph matched the sketchbook.

Humphries also says the newly surfaced diary contains about 162 notebook pages and came with excerpts from destroyed North West Company papers, journals, and letters. He describes Astra’s role as an end-to-end research assistant that searched forward from the artwork and backward through the historical record, while Humphries restricted access to the relevant documents.
developments.why_it_matters: Researchers can now evaluate Astra beyond benchmarks by checking whether its archival leads produce primary evidence whose handwriting, dates, and itinerary align.

developments.title: Superlogical Rex beta offers macOS app and Linux, FreeBSD, and Windows server builds
detail: Daniel Miessler describes Superlogical's Rex as a unified system for using AI across terminals, applications, TUIs, and orchestration, positioning it as an alternative to separate Electron, orchestrator, and terminal tools.
Rex's installation documentation says the project is in beta, with a macOS application and Linux, FreeBSD, and Windows server available to testers.
developments.why_it_matters: Linux and FreeBSD testers can install the server beta and evaluate whether one interface can cover several AI workflows they currently split across tools.

developments.title: Gemini 4 Carbon becomes available with Google AI Pro
detail: Rashmi Banthia reports that Gemini 4 Carbon is now available with the Google AI Pro plan. The supplied post does not specify the model’s capabilities, rollout scope, usage limits, or separate pricing.
developments.why_it_matters: Google AI Pro subscribers can now access Gemini 4 Carbon through their existing subscription without a separate purchase.

developments.title: LlamaIndex launches OCRia-1 for image-based document parsing
detail: LlamaIndex launched OCRia-1, a 4B document-parsing language model based on Qwen. OCRia-1 converts document images into Markdown while retaining tables and charts. Ollama published a direct model-pull command for adding OCRia-1 to document-processing workflows.
developments.why_it_matters: Ollama-based workflows can now normalize image-only documents into machine-readable Markdown without separately building OCR, table, and chart extraction steps.

developments.title: Joel forks T3 Code as J3 Code ahead of source closure
detail: Theo said T3 Code's source will close tonight and criticized the community's handling of the open-source project. Joel announced that he is forking T3 Code as J3 Code while the source is still available.
The supplied evidence does not identify a repository, release plan, license terms, compatibility guarantees, or maintainer for J3 Code.
developments.why_it_matters: Users needing continued access to T3 Code's source should check whether J3 Code provides a usable, licensed alternative before tonight's closure.

developments.title: Theo removes invasive telemetry from T3 Code
detail: Theo says he has removed all invasive telemetry from T3 Code and shared a pull request with the change. The quoted announcement does not name the affected telemetry, specify implementation details, or state when the change will ship.
developments.why_it_matters: T3 Code users can inspect Theo’s pull request to determine which telemetry paths were eliminated rather than assuming every form of data collection was removed.

developments.title: Claude adds installable desktop apps for artifacts
detail: Claude artifacts can now be installed as desktop apps on Mac and Windows. Users can ask Claude to build an artifact, select “Install as app,” and launch the result like a regular desktop application. Installed artifacts can use Claude connectors and, with user permission, send notifications or add a menu bar item.
developments.why_it_matters: Claude users can keep connector-enabled tools available outside the chat interface while controlling notification and menu-bar access.

developments.title: dot claims solutions to 55 conjectures
detail: The quoted claim says that “dot” solved 55 additional conjectures overnight, while Christopher D. Long identifies eight named examples: Haralambis, Pomerance–Sárközy, Minc Problem 18, Ma–Tang, Németh–Seery–Shu, Féray, Nuttall, and Bernardi–Morales.

Christopher D. Long characterizes several of the results as significant conjectures. The supplied evidence does not identify dot’s implementation, provide proofs, or document independent verification.
developments.why_it_matters: Researchers can use the named cases as a verification queue, but must not treat the 55 solutions as established without proofs or independent checks.

developments.title: Codex cuts process-launch latency under high parent memory
detail: Charlie Marsh reports that Codex now spawns processes much faster when its app server is using significant memory. In a macOS example with 20 GB of resident memory in the parent, per-launch time fell from about 200 ms to about 0.25 ms, an approximately 800x improvement.
developments.why_it_matters: Codex operators can benchmark parent resident memory when tuning agent infrastructure, since the reported launch time changes by about 800x under high-memory conditions.

developments.title: Inkling 2 Mini tops key coding benchmark categories
detail: Victor Mustar reports that Inkling 2 Mini evaluation results were posted on Hugging Face. The results place it first among models under 32B parameters on DeepSWE (48.2%) and under 128B on SWE-bench Verified (79.2%).
The results also place Inkling 2 Mini second in the under-32B Terminal-Bench 2.1 category (71.6%, using Pi) and second overall on SWE-bench Pro Hard (77.9%).
developments.why_it_matters: Named benchmark scores let readers compare Inkling 2 Mini’s coding-agent performance with similarly sized models.

developments.title: Pi Desktop adds pi-durable for IDE work inside an ADE
detail: Pi announced pi-durable in Pi Desktop, crediting Cristina Poncela as its builder. Pi describes it as an IDE embedded in an ADE, without specifying its individual editing, terminal, or agent features.
developments.why_it_matters: Pi Desktop users can perform IDE-style work within the agent environment instead of switching to a separate editor.

developments.title: Conductor moves its frontend to Electron while retaining its Rust server
detail: Charlie Holtz reports that Conductor rebuilt its frontend in Electron while keeping its Rust local server. Conductor reports 71% faster workspace opening, 4.6-times faster startup-to-render performance, and 35% less RAM use.
The rewrite increases Conductor's download size from roughly 200 MB to 500 MB.
developments.why_it_matters: Conductor users gain faster startup and lower memory use, but must account for the substantially larger installation download.

developments.title: Anthropic’s “Working with AI” paper examines AI adoption at 58 Claude-using companies
detail: Anthropic’s “Working with AI” paper draws on interviews with people at 58 companies using Claude about how AI is changing their work. It reports few layoffs but reduced hiring, with the most valuable AI uses often involving reorganizing roles and workplaces around the technology.
Daniel Miessler interprets the findings as arguing that organizational clarity and effective integration—not simply access to an AI system—drive gains from AI.
developments.why_it_matters: Organizations adopting Claude can now assess role and workplace redesign alongside model access when evaluating productivity gains.

developments.title: Jakub Antalik releases a cursor-emotion model for adaptive interfaces
detail: Jakub Antalik built a small model that analyzes cursor movement, velocity, and user interactions to recognize confusion, frustration, and disorientation. He says the model is ready in beta and free to use, positioning it as an input for generative or adaptive user interfaces.
The release provides a concrete way to test behavior-based emotion recognition without requiring explicit user feedback.
developments.why_it_matters: Developers can use the free beta to test whether interface systems can react to cursor-derived frustration or confusion.

developments.title: Astra 6.2 and Sol 6.2 Lead Karpathy Wiki Bench, Beating Opus 5.5
detail: Josh reports starting work on a Karpathy‑Wiki‑Bench using Opentrawl and notes that the Astra 6.2 and Sol 6.2 models placed first, surpassing Opus 5.5.
The benchmark evaluates models on building personal wikis from a user's data, highlighting strengths in data integration and retrieval.
developments.why_it_matters: Choose Astra 6.2 or Sol 6.2 for personal‑wiki tasks, as they outperform Opus 5.5 on this benchmark, indicating better data‑driven summarization.

developments.title: Simon Willison identifies three LLM capability inflection points
detail: Simon Willison published “Three LLM inflection points in twelve months,” expanding on his keynote at the AI Engineer summit.

He argues that LLM abilities have passed three significant inflection points over the past year, although the supplied excerpt does not name the inflection points or provide their supporting examples.
developments.why_it_matters: Readers can use Willison’s three-part framework to separate major LLM capability shifts from ordinary model updates when evaluating the past year.

external_links.title: Three LLM inflection points in twelve months

developments.title: Drew Breunig's "Using AI Without Losing Your Humanity" argues for preserving AI-output diversity
detail: Drew Breunig published a write-up of a recent talk about the human role when working with AI. Breunig argues that models trade diversity for reliability and says people should act as an irritant that pushes them beyond the model's paved path.
developments.why_it_matters: AI practitioners should review outputs for convergence on generic answers and deliberately test less typical alternatives instead of treating the default response as final.

external_links.title: Using AI Without Losing Your Humanity

developments.title: Unsloth Desktop unifies x64 and ARM64 Windows builds and adds package-manager installs
detail: Daniel Han says Unsloth Desktop now combines its x64 and ARM64 Windows binaries into a single executable, covering ARM64 systems such as RTX Spark machines.
Unsloth Desktop is also available through WinGet and Homebrew, with Han providing installation commands for both package managers.
developments.why_it_matters: Choosing one build removes architecture-specific download decisions, and WinGet or Homebrew users can install Unsloth without manually locating an executable.

developments.title: Sakana AI announces Namazu Small 30B model
detail: Sakana AI announced Namazu Small, a 30B-parameter model based on NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Nano and developed through continued pretraining and post-training.

Sakana reports that Namazu Small averaged stronger results than a roughly four-times-larger 120B model across 25 benchmarks. It says the model is particularly capable at long-form reading and research using web search, with on-premises deployment details expected in early December.
developments.why_it_matters: Local-inference teams can add Namazu Small to evaluation plans for document analysis and web research while awaiting its on-premises details.

developments.title: LingSante-3.1-air-VL quantized model flags synthetic clinical errors
detail: Alexey Fateev quantized the 124 B‑parameter LingSante-3.1-air-VL model to INT4 (W4A16) and ran it locally on a 4 × RTX 3090 rig using SGLang 0.5.23.
In three independent runs the model identified all ten deliberately inserted medication, lab, and imaging errors in a synthetic discharge packet for a 71‑year‑old patient.
Each full run processed 7.5‑10 K tokens in 64‑82 seconds (~123 tok/s), demonstrating fast, on‑premise error detection without cloud exposure.
developments.why_it_matters: You can audit discharge summaries locally with a privacy‑preserving LLM, catching medication and lab mistakes in under 90 seconds per case.

developments.title: tinygrad adds slopkernels for Python-generated AMD LLM kernels
detail: The tinygrad repository now includes a slopkernels directory with Python-generated AMD LLM kernels that output tinygrad UIR. The tiny corp says Neon is working to improve the kernels, testing whether the minimalist generation approach can extend their performance.
developments.why_it_matters: AMD-focused developers can now inspect and test the Python-to-tinygrad UIR path, using the initial repository version as a baseline while Neon improves the kernels.

developments.title: Dax moves Kimi inference traffic to self-operated GPUs
detail: Dax says all of their current Kimi traffic is now served from GPUs they operate. They report more efficient serving than any other provider and state that the deployment is not quantized.
developments.why_it_matters: The deployment gives readers a self-hosted option for evaluating Kimi inference without depending on an external provider.

developments.title: Astra 6.2 used in first deterministic linear-time minimum spanning tree algorithm
detail: Louie Putterman, Sanjeev Khanna, and Junkai Song at NYU report that their work using Astra 6.2 produced the first deterministic linear-time algorithm for minimum spanning tree. Putterman says the result completely settles the problem’s deterministic complexity.
developments.why_it_matters: The result can serve as a concrete benchmark for evaluating models that derive new deterministic algorithms.

developments.title: T3 Code telemetry collected Codex and Claude identifiers
detail: According to the cited T3 Code pull requests, PR #174 enabled PostHog telemetry by default and used a hashed account identifier derived from ~/.codex/auth.json; PR #1249 added a Claude Code identifier fallback.

PR #15028 reportedly routed payloads through T3 Tools' ingest server for raw archiving, while PR #21506 added Identify.ts to read the OpenAI user_id and Claude accountUuid from local files for hashing and cross-machine linking. Julius Marminge reportedly rejected a simpler opt-out in issue #1397, and community PR #27077's settings toggle and CLI switch were closed as unwanted.
The quoted code analysis does not show that authentication credentials were transmitted; it documents identifier collection and telemetry routing rather than credential theft.
developments.why_it_matters: EU users can request their T3 Tools telemetry records under GDPR Article 15 and should not attach authentication files, tokens, or keys.
